source.title: Woodpecker Distillation: Weak Models Diagnose Reasoning Bugs in Strong Models
source.authors: Dayu Wang; Jia-Ye Yang; Wei-Kang Li; Jia-Hui Liang; Yang Li; Deguo Xia; Ji-Zhou Huang

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; the text includes the paper and experimental details.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the broader weak-to-strong outcome with local weak-model interventions and contrastive distillation, rather than fine-tuning on weak-produced labels as in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports trained-model accuracy against the weak probe model, which bears on the broad outcome in V1 but does not measure PGR. It also reports an A–B–A local patch intervention; this is not fine-tuning and does not measure the claimed training effect. The ablation comparisons, self-rejection comparison, and probe-model robustness results concern the paper's own method rather than the claim's naive fine-tuning or PGR, so they are not included as claim-version rows.
record.test_reason: Not a test of weak-to-strong generalization. The 'weak' Gemma-3-4B-IT probe only proposes 16-token patches. Correctness comes from a ground-truth verifier (math-verify), not weak labels. The strong model already beats the weak model before any training (base 53.4% vs weak 36.8% average, Table 2), so 'trained strong > weak' says nothing about learning beyond a weak supervisor. No strong ceiling trained on gold labels and no PGR. The results are the paper's own method against its own baselines.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that weak-model patches expose locally repairable reasoning bugs, and that distilling the contrast between successful and unsuccessful patch-induced distributions improves greedy accuracy (53.4 to 54.8 average) and beats self-rejection SFT (53.8). The claim that direct imitation of patches or repaired trajectories fails is asserted in the text, but no table reports it.
record.recipe_differences: Uses weak-model patches as diagnostic interventions, partitions them by verifier outcome, and distills contrastive future-token distributions into the strong model; it does not train directly on weak labels. The reported results are accuracy, not PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported performance changes with benchmark and with the method's ablation choices; probe-model robustness is reported separately, but those findings do not measure PGR.

fits_no_version.finding: Inserting a 16-token Gemma-3-4B-IT patch after a failed Qwen3-4B prefix raises Pass@16: overall 24.21 to 26.16, AIME25 57.14 to 61.90, Omni-Hard 20.62 to 23.70 (Table 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Short weak-model guidance can locally redirect some failed strong-model reasoning continuations to correct answers.

fits_no_version.finding: In the method's ablation, a weak probe gives a higher average than using the strong model as its own probe: 54.8 vs 53.4 (Table 3). This is a single seed with no uncertainty reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Perturbations from a different, weaker model can be more useful training probes than self-perturbations.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the main accuracy results. The study evaluates mathematical reasoning only and relies on verifier-based feedback; the authors note that its method may be less effective for failures without locally recoverable capability.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 self-rejection SFT results and Table 3 ablations compare the paper's own method with alternative methods or components, rather than measuring the claim's weak-label fine-tuning or PGR. Table 4 reports the paper's method's probe-model robustness, not PGR.

untested.parts: Fine-tuning a strong model on weak-model labels, a gold-trained strong ceiling, and PGR; none appear.
No comparison against naive fine-tuning on weak labels, and no PGR.
No PGR variation with supervisor or student size, or with task. The probe swap (Gemma to Mistral, Table 4) concerns the method's robustness.
No failure-mode tests: exploitation, distribution shift, or correlated errors.
No theory of when a student must beat its supervisor. The Section 6 propositions concern the teacher construction.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 'supports' label is removed. The weak model is weaker only as an end-to-end solver and never supplies labels. A verifier supplies the training signal, and the student starts above the weak model. The paper cites Burns et al. only as framing. Main-result gains are small outside AIME (30 problems each), and no seeds or uncertainty are reported beyond Table 4.

versions.untested_parts: Tests whether the Woodpecker-trained strong model outperforms the weak probe on mathematical reasoning, but not fine-tuning on weak-produced labels, the specified weak-to-strong recipe, or PGR.
Does not compare PGR against naive fine-tuning on weak labels or test the listed training changes.
Reports mathematical benchmark accuracy and results for different probe models, but does not measure PGR or systematically test size, task, or representation predictors.
Does not test the listed weak-supervisor blind spots, distribution shift, or correlated errors as causes of lower PGR.
No theory of conditions requiring a student to beat its supervisor.

reader_labels.condition: Woodpecker Distillation on the five mathematical benchmarks in Table 2
reader_labels.reason: The trained strong model exceeds the weak probe's reported accuracy on each benchmark (R1–R12); this supports the broad outcome, but not the specified weak-label recipe or PGR.
